intro.text:
The headings below show the key information related to thunderstorms.

Click on each heading to view more information.

info.text:
• A small scale weather pattern or storm produced by the formation of cumulonimbus clouds, resulting in thunder, lightning, gusty winds and precipitation
  • Pose a significant hazard to aviation
  • Most frequently impact summer flying

For a thunderstorm to form, the air must have three things:
  • Sufficient water vapor
  • Unstable lapse rate
  • Upward/lifting mechanism

The physical attributes of a thunderstorm vary dramatically:
  • Diameter range: Less than 5 miles to more than 30 miles
  • Cloud bases from a few hundred feet to 10,000ft or higher
  • Tops range from 25,000ft to 45,000ft

    - Occasionally extend above 65,000ft



The wide variance in coverage and intensity of thunderstorms only increases the danger of known hazards
